source: synthetic. The bare [y/n] question upstream's `weak_blocker` is the
        last resort for, transcribed from that rule's own first literal rather
        than captured: a tool asking for confirmation in its own output, with
        no Codex prompt marker on screen and none of the control lines
        `live_strong_blocker` or `sidecar.approval_blocker` are gated on.
why: this is the fixture the `weak_blocker` overlay is kept for. Upstream
     declares the rule blocked with no `visible_blocker`, so the pane lands on
     the blocked lane with no attention flag and every surface that keys an
     alert on `Tracker.VisibleBlocker` stays quiet — which before the manifest
     cutover it did not. The overlay in manifests/sidecar/codex.toml replaces
     the rule by id, verbatim plus `visible_blocker = true`, so the verdict and
     the rule id are unchanged and only the nag comes back.
     The screen deliberately carries no `›` line: `weak_blocker`'s region is
     `whole_recent_without_current_prompt_marker`, which is empty whenever a
     current Codex prompt marker is on screen.
